sources_checked: https://www.getjobber.com/home-service-trends-report/: 1,050 US home service business owners, run through Conjointly in December 2025, margin of error +/-3 points at 90% confidence. 'Last year, 65% of businesses raised their prices.' HVAC 83%, plumbing 74%, electrical 74%, roofing 74%, general contracting 71.1%, and cleaning 'only 55% raised prices last year, the lowest of any trade.' Every trade with a figure is at 55% or more, so 'most trades raised their prices last year' holds. 'Inflation (72%) and labor costs (50%) are the most common reasons for price increases' (the chart labels the 72% 'inflation and material costs'). The page gives no size of increase, no customer reaction and no pricing plans, and the video claims none of these.

https://www.bls.gov/news.release/eci.htm: Employment Cost Index, June 2026, USDL-26-1270, released Fri Jul 31, 2026. Table 8, civilian wages and salaries, not seasonally adjusted, 12 months ending June 2026: all workers 3.2%; installation, maintenance, and repair 3.7%; construction, extraction, farming, fishing, and forestry 3.9%. 'Install and repair pay rose three point seven percent in the year to June' and 'your crew's pay beat the three point two for all workers' both hold, the construction row (3.9) included. The plate reads 'BLS, 12 months to June 2026'.

https://www.getjobber.com/: page title 'The Top Home & Commercial Service Software in 2026 | Jobber', field service software for quoting, scheduling, invoicing and payments, which supports 'Jobber sells software'.
